Product:{\"sku\":\"7100133738\"}.description({\"html\":true}):
CARTAGRA, the original debut work from Innocent Grey, renowned for numerous mystery visual novels, comes to Nintendo Switch™!
In Ueno, Tokyo, where the wounds of the Pacific War have not yet fully healed, Detective Takashiro Shugo becomes embroiled in a bizarre serial murder case.
A story of love and hate that twists into obsession and madness...

Nintendo Switch Edition Features
A console version of the remade game featuring refined graphics and music. Also includes the epilogue, "Sacrament."

New CG events illustrated by Sugina Miki. Stunning visuals bring new life to iconic scenes.

Experience the game in Full HD (1980 x 1080) in TV mode. Enjoy the beautiful visuals in stunning high definition.

Fully voice acted, including the protagonist. The talented voice cast bring the story to life with their passionate performances.

The text can be set to English, Simplified Chinese, or Japanese (audio is in Japanese only).
This includes in-game text, options, and the digital manual. Language settings can be changed at any time.

Touch screen controls and Nintendo Switch™ Lite are also supported.

Game System
Gameplay in this choice-based visual novel involves reading through the story while making choices at certain key points. Different decisions may lead to different outcomes, story branches and endings.

Story
The Showa era. Several years after the war, a series of gruesome murders are causing unrest among the population. Takashiro Shugo, former member of the Metropolitan Police Department, is asked to investigate a missing persons case by his former boss, Arishima Kazuma.
Written on the request is the name "Kozuki Yura," the same name as Takashiro's former lover.

Yura's father, Kozuki Keiichiro, tells Shugo: "You see, my daughter, Yura is... already dead."

Truth and fiction interweave. Before long, the connection between the two incidents comes to light.
With Ueno as the backdrop, the curtain rises on a tragedy...

Staff
Illustration: Sugina Miki
Story: Sudukamiya/Iida Kazuhiko (Original Story)
Music: MANYO
